verses.1: A contemplation of David, when he was in the cave. A prayer.
verses.2: My voice cries out to the LORD; my voice begs the LORD.
verses.3: I pour out my plea before him; I tell him my distress.
verses.4: When my spirit is overwhelmed within me, you alone know my path. In this way I walk; they have hidden a trap for me.
verses.5: I looked to my right and saw, but no one knew me; there is no one who seeks my life.
verses.6: I cried to you, O LORD, and said: "You are my refuge, my portion in the land of the living."
verses.7: Hear my plea, for I am greatly humbled; deliver me from those who pursue me, for they are too strong for me.
verses.8: Bring my soul out from prison, that I may praise your name. Let the righteous surround me, for you will repay me.

notes:
Notes
- v. 1: "A contemplation" (maskil) is a poetic or didactic psalm. The phrase "when he was in the cave" is a marginal note in the Hebrew and is not part of the actual title structure. It is retained here for clarity.

[1] A contemplation of David, when he was in the cave. A prayer.

[2] My voice cries out to the LORD; my voice begs the LORD.

[3] I pour out my plea before him; I tell him my distress.

[4] When my spirit is overwhelmed within me, you alone know my path. In this way I walk; they have hidden a trap for me.

[5] I looked to my right and saw, but no one knew me; there is no one who seeks my life.

[6] I cried to you, O LORD, and said: "You are my refuge, my portion in the land of the living."

[7] Hear my plea, for I am greatly humbled; deliver me from those who pursue me, for they are too strong for me.

[8] Bring my soul out from prison, that I may praise your name. Let the righteous surround me, for you will repay me.
